How Much Does IKEA Kitchen Fitting Cost?

31 July 2026·BMB Renovation

If you are planning an IKEA kitchen, the price of the cabinets and appliances is only part of the budget. You may also need to allow for installation labour, removing the old kitchen, plumbing, electrics, worktop fitting, waste disposal and any adjustments needed to make standard units work in your room. So, how much does IKEA kitchen fitting cost in the UK? As a rough guide, fitting labour for a straightforward kitchen may typically be around £2,000 to £5,000, excluding the kitchen itself. More involved projects can cost considerably more, particularly where the layout is changing or the room needs preparation. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

Typical IKEA kitchen fitting costs

There is no single IKEA installation price because every kitchen has a different number of units, appliances, worktops and service requirements. A small, simple kitchen with the same layout may sit towards the lower end of a fitting range. A larger kitchen with an island, integrated appliances, bespoke panels or a new layout can take longer and require more work. As a broad budgeting guide, you might allow the following rough typical UK ranges rather than treating them as fixed prices. Every project differs, so request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing:

  • Basic cabinet and drawer assembly and installation: as a rough guide, typically around £1,500 to £3,500.
  • More complex cabinet fitting, panels, islands and adjustments: as a rough guide, typically around £3,000 to £6,000 or more.
  • Worktop fitting: as a rough guide, often around £300 to £1,000, depending on the material, joins, cut-outs and edge details.
  • Removal of the existing kitchen and disposal: as a rough guide, typically around £300 to £800.
  • Plumbing and electrical work: as a rough guide, potentially around £500 to £2,000 or more, depending on what is being moved or added.

What does the installation labour include?

A fitting quote should explain exactly what is included. Cabinet installation may cover assembling IKEA units, levelling base cabinets, securing wall units, fitting doors and drawers, installing plinths and attaching cover panels. It may also include fitting handles and preparing units for appliances. However, the worktop, sink, tap and appliances may be priced separately, especially if specialist cutting or connections are required.

Plumbing, electrics and appliance connections

Plumbing requirements often depend on whether the sink, dishwasher, washing machine or refrigerator stays in its existing position. Keeping services where they are may reduce labour, while moving a sink or appliance can involve extending pipework, altering waste runs and making good the wall or floor. Check whether the quote includes connection of appliances, isolation valves, new pipework and testing, rather than assuming these are part of cabinet fitting.

Electrical work can include extra sockets, relocated sockets, cooker supplies, lighting, extractor connections and wiring for integrated appliances. The cost will depend on access, the existing installation and the number of changes required. If you are comparing quotes for a project in Watford or nearby, a detailed kitchen fitting service quote should separate cabinet work from plumbing and electrical items so that the total is easier to understand.

Common extra charges to budget for

  • Removing and disposing of the old kitchen, flooring, tiles or wall coverings.
  • Repairing uneven walls, floors or ceilings before cabinets can be installed accurately.
  • Changing gas, water or waste positions because the new layout differs from the old one.
  • Additional electrical sockets, lighting, extractor work or appliance circuits.
  • Worktop cut-outs for sinks and hobs, particularly with laminate, timber, quartz or other specialist materials.
  • End panels, filler panels, decorative trim and custom alterations where standard IKEA dimensions do not suit the room.
  • New flooring, splashbacks, tiling, decorating and making good after services are moved.
  • Unexpected issues such as damaged pipework, damp, concealed wiring or a floor that needs levelling.

Why IKEA kitchen adjustments can affect the price

IKEA units are designed around standard sizes, but kitchens may have walls or dimensions that require adjustment. Filler panels may be needed beside walls, doors can require careful alignment and a cabinet may need adapting around pipework. Tall housings, corner units and integrated appliances also require accurate measurements. These details can add time even when the kitchen itself is relatively small.

The worktop can be another significant variable. Laminate worktops may be cut and joined on site, while timber needs appropriate treatment and stone or composite worktops may involve specialist templating and fabrication. Ask whether the quote includes delivery, carrying materials into the property, cut-outs, joins, upstands and sealing.

How to compare IKEA kitchen fitting quotes

The cheapest quote is not necessarily the lowest final cost if important items are excluded. Ask each fitter for a written breakdown covering cabinet assembly, installation, worktops, appliances, plumbing, electrics, tiling, flooring, decorating, waste removal and making good. Confirm whether VAT applies, how variations are handled and who supplies fixings, trims and finishing materials.

It is also sensible to clarify the preparation expected before work starts. For example, will the room need to be empty, will the existing kitchen be removed by the fitter and will the floor be ready for the new units? A site visit can help identify awkward access, uneven surfaces and service changes before a price is agreed. A realistic budget for your project

For a straightforward IKEA kitchen where the layout stays broadly the same, a total fitting budget of roughly £2,000 to £5,000 may be a useful starting point, excluding cabinets, appliances and some materials. For a full renovation involving removal, new flooring, tiling, relocated services, lighting, worktops and decorating, fitting and associated work may typically be around £5,000 to £10,000 or more. These are only rough planning ranges: room size, access, specification, location and the condition of the existing kitchen can all change the final cost. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does IKEA kitchen fitting cost in the UK?+
As a rough guide, fitting labour may typically cost around £2,000 to £5,000, excluding the kitchen. Complex layouts or additional renovation work can take the total above this range. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
Does IKEA kitchen installation include plumbing and electrics?+
Not always. Some fitting quotes cover cabinets only, while plumbing, electrical work, appliance connections and lighting are priced separately. Check the written quotation carefully.
Is it cheaper to fit an IKEA kitchen yourself?+
DIY fitting may reduce labour costs, but some parts of the project may still require professional tradespeople, such as electrical, gas or specialist plumbing work. Consider the tools, time and experience needed before deciding.
What is usually not included in an IKEA kitchen fitting quote?+
Common exclusions can include kitchen units, appliances, worktops, old-kitchen disposal, flooring, tiling, decorating, service alterations and specialist worktop fabrication. Always request an itemised quote.
How can I reduce the cost of fitting an IKEA kitchen?+
Keeping the existing layout and service positions may reduce labour. You can also compare itemised quotes, choose a suitable worktop and decide in advance which preparation or finishing tasks you will complete yourself.
